sentences.text:
M.Kamala vs State Of Telangana, on 7 August, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner, seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a Writ, Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS declaring the action of the respondent authorities in not considering the application/petitions filed by the petitioner regarding the compensation ex-gratia to be paid and other benefits for the land acquired in Sy.No.961/3 at Tadicherla village, Malaharao mandal, Karimnagar District as illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional and consequently direct the respondents to pay the compensation ex-gratia to the petitioner for the land admeasuring Ac.4.00 in Sy.No.961/3 at Tadicherla village,
Malaharao Mandal, Karimnagar District and grant other benefits of rehabilitation resettlement under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, Act, 30/2013 and pass..."

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, Act, 30/2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri K. S. Murthy, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Sri P. Sri Harsha Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for Singareni Collieries Company Limited appearing for respondent No.8 and perused the record.
3.
The case of the petitioner is that her husband was given Ac.5.00 of land by the Government as he is a landless poor person.

After his demise in the year 2010, the revenue authorities have issued pattadar passbook to the petitioner under the provisions of record of rights pattadar passbooks Act,
1971, vide passbook No.1705, dated 14.12.2011 for the land admeasuring Ac.4.00 in Sy.No.961/3 of Tadicherla village, Karimnagar District.
Since the date of issuance of the pattadar passbook, the petitioner is in enjoyment and possession of the said land.

4. The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent- authorities without initiating the proceedings under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013 are making efforts to forcibly dispossess her from the said land.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. Sri K. S. Murthy, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the respondent-authorities had rejected the application made by the petitioner regarding the compensation/ex-gratia to be paid and other benefits for the land acquired in Sy.No.961/3 and they are forcibly dispossessing the petitioner from the said land.
Learned counsel seeks a direction to the respondents to examine the application submitted by the petitioner along with the title documents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Sri P. Sri Harsha Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for Singareni Collieries Company Limited appearing for respondent No.8 submitted that upon verification of the documents filed in support of the claim made in respect of the subject land in Sy.No.961/3, the compensation amount has been paid.

7. While the respondents submitted that they have paid the compensation, the petitioner has stated that no compensation has been received for the land for which forcible possession has taken place by the respondents, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the respondents to consider and dispose of the application made by the petitioner and if it is found that no compensation has been paid, the respondents are directed to take appropriate steps in accordance with law, if the petitioner is entitled to receive compensation, within a period of three (03) months from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.
8. With the above observations/directions this writ petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

__ __ C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J Date: 07.08.2024 vsu M.Kamala vs State Of Telangana, on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119737948/
